title: Normalized clopen exceptional comparisons at all coefficients
statement: Fix the purity datum [def-pur-conventions]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism between finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $c$ be a compactification of $g$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], and let $j:X_i\to X$ be an open and closed immersion with $X_i$ of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-open-immersion] [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Use the coefficient operations and units [def-pur-clopen-coefficient-operations]. Define the normalized exceptional comparison data as follows. At a finite coefficient field, the data consist of the actual strict etale compact-support and exceptional adjoints, their normalized clopen restriction comparison [def-pur-clopen-strict-system-comparison], the etale/pro-etale and sequence-site comparison, and finite evaluations of this same system comparison. Finite exceptional functors are those of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]; their component maps are the counit-normalized right-adjoint comparisons for component insertion and compact support. The integral exceptional functors are both compact-support right adjoints and the actual sequence-limit realizations of these strict systems; the integral restriction comparison is the image of the specified system map. Rational comparisons are their images under rationalization, fixed on every pure tensor. Include the finite-adjoint data, its normalization predicate and their combined structure, and similarly the single-field coefficient data, its coherence predicate and their combined structure. The all-coefficients data consist of this package at the fixed field and every finite stage of the fixed algebraic closure, the compact-support coefficient actions [def-weil-compact-support-coefficient-action], their exceptional right-adjoint actions and stagewise restriction comparisons. Its coherence predicate identifies the stage actions and adjunctions with the single-field packages, fixes transition maps as counit mates including identity extensions, and fixes the common-stage comparison by the displayed stage representative. The combined structure is the data together with this predicate. The four dualizing-unit comparisons are obtained by evaluating these same finite, integral, rational and common-stage comparisons on their coefficient units. These definitions record data and equations only; they assert no existence of the comparison packages.
